correctness.rationale: The center-reduction lemma forces a maximum abelian subalgebra to contain all n central edge basis elements. For a commuting dimension-a subspace, adjacent vertex-coordinate functionals are dependent; each occupied cyclic run contributes at most one independent direction, giving a<=floor(n/2). Equality forces exactly a supported runs, and binary-run length sum forces alternating support for even cycles, or a unique double run for odd cycles. These give precisely two points or n parametrized projective lines with specified intersection nodes. The Grassmannian Plücker embedding makes each a reduced projective line, and transversality gives ordinary nodes; all components defined over any field. Finite-field inclusion-exclusion produces n q. Exhaustive RREF verification agrees in nine cases.

value.rationale: The moduli of maximum-dimensional abelian Lie subalgebras is a natural equality stratum for the established independence-number dimension bound and encodes all simultaneous commuting vertex planes. An entire infinite family exhibits a sharp structural change: two isolated maxima versus a connected genus-one nodal cycle of n projective lines, with rational-point count n q. This is a complete geometric classification, not a routine rephrasing of a bound or a small finite enumeration; it opens comparisons with geometry of subalgebra schemes beyond cycles.
